questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a nice big city and CU had different courses than UCPH.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay. Charles University is less organised than UCPH, but it didn't give me much trouble - I found out along the way, and student information was good at helping in both CU and UCPH.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an orientation day where we got all information and a tour of the campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It wasn't difficult. I found a room through Student Republic, which was okay - not sure if I would recommend it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I had a good experience living off campus, but I think I would also have a good experience living on campus. You might hear some bad things about the housing provided by CU, but my impression is that it's also a great experience, and it's fun/nice living with other students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was good. We got the schedule of the courses just before starting, which was a bit late. I had a few courses that overlapped, so I had to find other, but you had the first 2 weeks to try out all courses, which was really nice!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You started the courses from your Learning Agreement, and you could also try other courses that you considered. After about 2 weeks you had to go to the Erasmus Office if you wanted to change your Learning Agreement.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't know. I didn't research it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful. I wanted to register for a course at another faculty which i couldn't because Czech students had priority, but I had friends that were successful in registering for courses at other faculties.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try out different courses in the first weeks.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I liked that CU had courses in geographic disciplines that UCPH don't have, like political geography and demography. In general the level was lower than at UCPH and the structure is way different, but it was really nice to gain new perspectives.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Generally lower than at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UCPH the teaching and examination is way more structured than at CU. There isn't really a typical way of teaching, so the teachers choose it themselves. It could be frustrating at times when you are used to something so structured as UCPH, but in the end it was a really valuable experience and nice to gain new perspectives.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Flood Risk Management
Fundamentals of Demography
High-impact Weather Phenomena
Open Source GIS
Special Topics in Political Geography
4EU+ Soil mechanics I

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Open Source GIS was nice and chill. Special Topics in Political Geography is a really good course, if you are interested in such fields/topics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think I had any.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport is very cheap and so good. Housing you can find cheaper, if you want - like the dorms from CU. In general Prague is much cheaper than Copenhagen, so I could eat more out, go to cafees and stuff like that.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Faculty of Science has a student club called Erasmus Club, where local student arrange activities and trips for exchange student - those are really good. CU also offers a lot of sport activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: In the start of the semester Erasmus Club arrange a trip - usually to a town called Bouzov. I would highly recommend to go there. It is a very good opportunity to meet people. They also arrange other fun activities and hikes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hang out in Prague, explore the city, go to other places in Czech Republic and go on hikes. Prague is also in the center of Europe and train tickets are not expensive, so it's a good opportunity to go to other places in Europe.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was not difficult. People mostly speak english and the city is easy to navigate through.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly hung with other international students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Maybe that less people speak English than in Denmark, and some people can be a bit rude when you don't speak Czech.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It is such a cool culture to explore. I didn't know much about Czech culture before going to Prague, so it has been so interesting to learn and to participate in cultural events and public holidays, for example Freedom and Democracy Day and St. Nicholas Day.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go on the Bouzov Trip arranged by Erasmus Club (and other events).
Be open-minded to different ways of teaching and examination.
Explore Prague and Czech Republic.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's a beautiful campus and Prague is a good exchange city with a lot of exchange students.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all over Europe and having an international friend group.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It can be challenging and hard at times because everything is new and unfamiliar.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
